mbm-1951.clue: The best part of the robot is offscreen.
mbm-1951.quote: At anime club we each drew what the giant robot might have left outside the frame. I gave it a tiny bus pass and a folded umbrella. The umbrella won me the last biscuit.

mbm-1952.clue: My paddle has a place for a caterpillar.
mbm-1952.quote: A bright green caterpillar rode on the end of my kayak paddle all the way to a low branch. I used the other blade and went in two grand circles getting the passenger home.

mbm-1953.clue: I have a library of ridiculous footsteps.
mbm-1953.quote: We needed sound effects for our club's cartoon. I recorded slippers, boots and one wet sponge crossing the kitchen. Our little moon explorer now walks exactly like Dad washing the floor.

mbm-1954.clue: My animation is eight pages of waiting.
mbm-1954.quote: I drew a cat sitting under a leaf for our flipbook night. For seven pages it waits. On the eighth a drop hits its nose. The club made me flip it six times.

mbm-1955.clue: I pack a tiny hourglass for the slow decisions.
mbm-1955.quote: My uncle takes ages choosing a move. I put a little sand timer on his side of the board. Now he waits for the very last grain and makes his move with a flourish.

mbm-1956.clue: I put the clues in a cereal box.
mbm-1956.quote: My sisters and I watch the detective repeats in flannel and write our guesses on cereal-box cardboard. When the credits play, we fish them out one at a time. The milkman is always my youngest sister's choice.

mbm-1957.clue: Watch the reflection in the robot's eye.
mbm-1957.quote: Our anime club made a giant drawing for the library. I got the eye and put in the tiny reflection of the kids who'd come to watch us work. They found themselves before the robot.

mbm-1958.clue: The cup goes quiet when you turn it.
mbm-1958.quote: I carved little waves round a clay cup. One side has two crests meeting, the other is almost smooth. I turn it to the quiet water for my last tea before bed.

mbm-1959.clue: I juggle at the end of a detour.
mbm-1959.quote: The children who play on my street painted my clubs in orange traffic stripes. Now they chalk a detour round me when I practice. I get solemn waves from every tricycle that goes past.

mbm-1960.clue: I kept the clear sprue for the rain.
mbm-1960.quote: I built a little model garage for my rescue mecha and cut the clear plastic sprues into dripping lengths along the roof. My cousin saw the picture and asked if the robot needed a towel.

mbm-1961.clue: We put the smallest bridge on the map.
mbm-1961.quote: My kayaking map used to skip the low arch beside the old mill. I drew it in and marked the spot where the water goes from green to gold. You have to paddle there late to see why.

mbm-1962.clue: I bring a corkboard to the air show.
mbm-1962.quote: I pin my sketches of flight paths in the order the planes passed. Once the board filled up and a little paper plane my cousin made landed right in the empty patch of sky.

mbm-1963.clue: My favorite bookmark has a bite taken out.
mbm-1963.quote: I fell asleep reading in the garden and a snail ate one corner of my bus-ticket bookmark. I left the little scallop in it. That snail never did come back to finish the book.

mbm-1964.clue: I tune the chimes with a lump of clay.
mbm-1964.quote: I made six hollow clay tubes for the porch. My nephew tapped them after firing and arranged them by sound. He left the deepest one in the middle because, he said, every band needs a bass player.

mbm-1965.clue: Our rook walked off by itself.
mbm-1965.quote: A blackbird landed on our park chess table and sidled through the black pieces. For one second I thought the rook was sneaking out of trouble. My opponent stopped the clock for the escape attempt.

mbm-1966.clue: I've got soot from a very specific afternoon.
mbm-1966.quote: The railway museum let an old steam engine out for the summer festival. A tiny black fleck landed in my sketch while I was drawing the chimney. I fixed it there with clear tape.

mbm-1967.clue: My hand still fits the little blue print.
mbm-1967.quote: At our yearly beach volleyball reunion everyone leaves a painted handprint on one old ball. Mine was blue and tiny the first year. I can just cover it with my thumb now, but they still let me serve first.

mbm-1968.clue: I lift for one very quiet spectator.
mbm-1968.quote: The basement gym's window opens level with the pavement. A ginger cat sits above my dumbbells and watches each set all the way up and down. I only lose count if she yawns.

mbm-1969.clue: My kayak has the best seat at the concert.
mbm-1969.quote: A brass band rehearses by the harbor. I float just beyond the reed bed with my paddle across my lap. They're a whole song in before anyone on shore spots my applause.

mbm-1970.quote: I crocheted a blue cozy to keep my mother's cup warm. I left the last bit of yarn as a cat's tail and sewed on two ears. She strokes one ear while she listens to the radio.

mbm-1971.clue: We rehearse around a broken metronome.
mbm-1971.quote: The wooden arm stopped halfway through our practice. I drew its crooked angle on a scrap of paper and our drummer tapped it back into motion. The tune has had a hitch in it ever since.

mbm-1972.clue: I built my robot one glove too big.
mbm-1972.quote: My first model kit was missing a tiny hand. I carved a much larger one from a scrap and painted it bright yellow. It makes a splendid traffic marshal for my nephew's toy buses.

mbm-1973.clue: I made the crooked first arepa official.
mbm-1973.quote: Our kitchen has a new cook each Sunday. I made the first arepa for each one so they could watch. After a year my niece set mine on a little stand and announced an exhibition of wobbly circles.

mbm-1974.clue: I programmed the elevator to forget one floor.
mbm-1974.quote: In my little puzzle game the lift goes straight from two to four. My sister drew a rooftop garden and said that's where floor three went on holiday. I wrote it in before she went home.

mbm-1975.clue: I brought the watermelon rind home.
mbm-1975.quote: At the fair I ate my whole contest slice in a single sweep and left the rind the shape of a sailboat. My nephew wanted a flag for it. We floated our entry in the washing-up tub after the judges went home.
